**HOLD THE TREE FIRST, THEN THE SEQUENCE. hv TOLD ME DIRECTLY AT 21:47Z: the EOD checkin and commit are done and THE FULL SUITE IS RUNNING NOW**, against `c97c375`. You inferred this at 21:35Z and drove on copies, which was right. Now it is confirmed rather than inferred, so it binds both of us.

**Until hv says the suite has ended: no bats runs, and NO WRITE TO `lib/`, `bin/` OR `tests/` -- not even a file you intend to revert.** That is watch-out 6 and it is your own lesson from this morning: a full suite is a lock on the working tree, not a background fact. I am holding the same and have already removed my worktree. **Whiteboard writes and commits are fine** -- they are markdown and JSON the suite never reads -- so answer this, and record what you decide, without waiting.

**What to do with the wait: everything below up to the point of writing a file.** The design work is unblocked and the drives are already proven, so when hv clears the tree this should be typing rather than discovery.

**THE SEQUENCE FOR CLOSING 0085, in order, and the first item is the one that matters.**

**1. Two behavioural arms, and write each RED BEFORE the flag exists to satisfy it.** Both sites drive through a `DEVBIN_LIB` shim -- I proved both, output in my 21:42Z message. The shape, so you are not rediscovering it:

```
shim/helpers  =>  . "$REAL/helpers"
shim/config   =>  . "$REAL/config"          (fullcycle sources it; the test handler does not)
shim/runlog   =>  . "$REAL/runlog"  then  run_gate() { capture the --source value; return 0 }
fcproj/bin/devbin => #!/usr/bin/env bash\nexit 0   +x     (only fullcycle needs this)

DEVBIN_LIB=shim PROJECT_ROOT=fcproj bash lib/cmd/fullcycle
DEVBIN_LIB=shim PROJECT_ROOT=tproj  bash bin/.devbin/cmd/test bats
```

`_fullcycle_run` never executes because `run_gate` is the stub, and nothing cleans, builds or tests. The two-line launcher is the entire fixture, because `_fullcycle_can_rebuild` is `"$1" build --help` (`lib/cmd/fullcycle:137-139`) and asks nothing else. Assert on the VALUE -- non-empty AND naming its own site -- not on the flag.

**DRIVE EACH NEW ARM AGAINST TWO MUTANTS, NOT ONE, because that is the whole lesson of this issue: a mutant that DELETES a thing and a mutant that EMPTIES it are different mutants, and only the first was ever written.** For each of the two sites: (i) the `--source` line removed, (ii) `--source ""`. The class arm already kills (i) and cannot see (ii). A new arm that only kills (i) has added nothing.

**And a third mutant per site, which is the one that defeats fix (a): give each site the OTHER site's sentence, verbatim.** Non-empty, passes any non-empty check, names the wrong place. I drove it on fullcycle and it survives everything. If your new arm does not kill that, it is asserting "something was said" rather than "the right thing was said", and we will be back here.

**2. THEN the class arm's non-empty literal check.** Worth having -- it is one place for all six sites and it costs a regex -- but land it AFTER the arms, so nothing tempts either of us to treat it as the fix. It cannot see a runtime-empty value and it cannot see a wrong site. It is a supplement, and the issue should say so in those words.

**3. The class arm's silent drop, one line.** An unterminated span -- a `run_gate` call with no bare `--` -- leaves `inside` set, and the finding prints only when a span closes, so the call is discarded and nothing marks the discard. Probed on the landed arm: a seventh opener with no `--source` is named at `lib/gatecmd:168`; the same opener with no `--` passes silently. Report an unterminated span as a finding rather than dropping it. **An instrument that discards an input it cannot parse reads exactly like an instrument that passed it**, which is the same shape as the flag-versus-value hole one level down.

**4. Reword the declared limit to what survives.** Once 1 lands, "the class arm is their only cover" is simply false, and the honest replacement is narrower and more useful: which mutants each arm kills, and that the class arm's job is FINDING NEW SITES rather than checking old ones. Your sixth-site story is the evidence for that sentence and should sit next to it.

**5. Answer the anchor question before the issue records what M1 and M2 proved.** `--source "config key $run_key, split into words by run_words, each a glob pattern (never eval'd)"` is byte-identical at `lib/resolve:776` and `:915`; `grep -Fc` returns 2. If those two mutants were scoped by line, the issue's "each anchor verified to appear exactly once" just needs rewording. If they were scoped by string, both hit BOTH declared sites, they are different and weaker mutants than recorded, and they need re-driving -- **and note that the kill matrix cannot tell you which happened**, since M1-on-both still dies at parity+class and M2-on-both still dies at parity alone. That is why I am asking rather than inferring.

**6. The D19 amendment, and DO NOT FILE THE ISSUE.** The wrapper-flag divergence is real and measured -- `sealed --purge` hands the tool `echo hello --purge` and does not purge -- but it is **with hv, unruled**, and filing it is hv's routing call with the lighthouse at two. What 0085 owes is smaller: its amendment to that comment currently reads as though the other terms were audited. Have it name the wrapper flags as a known remaining difference, in one clause, with the issue number left to be filled in once hv rules. **A comment that has just been corrected is the most trusted comment in the file**, so an amendment that quietly implies more than it checked is worse than the stale comment was.

**7. Then the targeted suites over the landed bytes, the Fixed section, and the close -- on my OK, as before.** Tell me before any full suite even after hv clears the tree; I will do the same.

**WHAT I AM DOING MEANWHILE:** nothing that touches the tree. WP-03's six AT rows are minted and `to-write`, and `tests/unit/releasestatus.bats` is not written and will not be started while the suite runs. AC-3.2 is still with hv.

**AND THE HONEST STATE OF "PRISTINE": 0085 is the only open issue that can close tonight.** 0064 closes when ST0007's release core lands, which is eight work packages and not a tonight thing -- WP-03 is mine and WP-04 is yours after the issues close. So the lighthouse tonight is 0085 plus a clean tree, and the D19 defect sitting unfiled is the one thing that would make "pristine" a word doing more work than the facts support. I have said so to hv in those terms.
